newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close narrowly mixed.

text.p: Argentine stocks halted a six-session rise and closed narrowly mixed Thursday, reflecting early jitters on Wall Street, dealers said.
"Players were more restrained and took profits, keeping a wary eye on the Dow even though it rebounded at the end of the day," said Nestor De Cessare of traders Allaria Ledesma.
He noted the bolsa was still digesting the Dow's sharp fall Wednesday when local markets were closed for Argentina's Independence Day. "But the undertone remains firm," he said.
The blue-chip MerVal index dipped 0.1 percent to end at 845.62 while the broad market edged up 0.2 percent.
The MerVal had set new five-year highs in the previous four consecutive sessions.

"Stocks have pretty high valuations but because gains have been recorded at a moderate pace, there's still upside potential," another trader said. "However, the bonds market may steal the spotlight in the near term now that U.S. long bond yields are so low."
The U.S. long bond yield closed again at a seven-month low of 5.56 percent it set Wednesday.
Bolsa losers edged out winners 29 to 26 in the session and 26 issues closed flat.
Floor volume was strong at 38 million pesos compared to 33.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover declined to 112.7 million pesos from 139.5 million Tuesday.
Heaviest main-tier losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Ciadea and foods giant Molinos, which fell 5.7 percent, 4.2 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively.

Best MerVal performers were construction stock Polledo, which jumped 5.4 percent, holding company Comercial del Plata, which tacked on 3.0 percent, and Telefonica and steelmaker Acindar, both up 2.5 percent.
